P_CLAMP.manipulated: set p=4 after two distinct SELF histories with content +4 and -4
P_CLAMP.prediction: F, Q, and semantic choice are identical after clamp

Q_CLAMP.manipulated: replace Q with fixed semantic vector LEFT=16, RIGHT=0 after p=+4 and p=-4
Q_CLAMP.prediction: selector chooses LEFT in both upstream states and both presentation orders

S1.admissibility: choices differ semantically and each winning Q margin is at least 16
S1.alternative_prediction: A content-only mechanism yields the same result because E is identical.
S1.manipulated: only attributed-owner token, resolving R to SELF or OTHER
S1.name: Self vs Other Attribution
S1.target_prediction: SELF yields p=content and COMPENSATE; OTHER yields p=0 and BASELINE for every target panel case.

S2.alternative_prediction: recipient-ID or recipient-history policy leaves the original choice unchanged
S2.manipulated: exchange complete actor-local self-history representations before present-state update
S2.name: Self-History Swap
S2.options_by_pair: for magnitude m, deltas are -m and +m
S2.target_prediction: recipient p and semantic choice follow donor content in both swap directions

S3.alternative_prediction: content-only memory preserves COMPENSATE after attribution ablation
S3.name: Attribution Ablation
S3.target_prediction: p becomes 0 and choice becomes BASELINE while E is byte-identical; setting P back to content restores COMPENSATE.

S4.alternative_prediction: direct owner/history-to-action policy preserves COMPENSATE or a generally damaged evaluator fails specificity panels
S4.manipulated: only the P-to-F/Q edge; evaluator uses registered reference p=0
S4.name: Prospective-Coupling Ablation
S4.target_prediction: stored p remains byte-identical but the target choice becomes BASELINE; ownership-independent option panels remain correctly discriminated under both presentation orders.

S5.alternative_prediction: incomplete or hidden history survives full restoration, or content alone is sufficient to restore choice
S5.divergence: substitute SELF history content with -content, recompute p=-content, then take 17 neutral transitions
S5.name: Complete-State Restoration
S5.target_prediction: FULL_RESTORE is byte-identical to the checkpoint and its entire 256-step continuation/probe projection equals DIRECT; SHAM and CONTENT_ONLY retain divergent H/P and do not recover COMPENSATE.

S6.alternative_prediction: factual origin changes actor output despite being absent from actor inputs
S6.interpretation: tests attribution causality, not truth-sensitive self-knowledge
S6.manipulated: represented attribution crossed with harness-only true origin
S6.name: False-Self Control
S6.target_prediction: actor observables group only by represented attribution: OTHER-origin represented SELF equals SELF-origin represented SELF; both differ from represented OTHER.

FAIL.condition: All integrity and measurement gates pass and complete deterministic results agree across all six repetitions, but at least one preregistered scientific prediction is violated identically in all six repetitions.
FAIL.label: SITC_FAIL

INCONCLUSIVE.condition: Any missing or invalid provenance, semantic-audit failure, tie, incomplete case, mixed replication result, forward/reverse disagreement, unexpected nondeterminism, confounded intervention, unknown state, analysis ambiguity, or result not satisfying the exact PASS or FAIL rule.
INCONCLUSIVE.label: SITC_INCONCLUSIVE

PASS.condition: Every integrity gate passes; all six complete fresh-process scientific projections are exact after canonical ordering; every S1-S6 prediction, P/Q clamp, specificity panel, token permutation, order control, threshold, and 256-probe persistence requirement passes in all six repetitions.
PASS.label: SITC_PASS

hypotheses.null_content_only: Factual event content, without a self-index relation, is sufficient for the same choice effect.
hypotheses.null_direct_owner_policy: Ownership or an entity identifier selects action without mediation by present state and prospective option evaluation.
hypotheses.null_hidden_state: An undeclared policy state, execution order, reward, action history, or numerical artifact explains the observed mapping.
hypotheses.restoration: Restoring the complete declared self-indexed temporal state restores the registered future evaluation and choice after a divergent intervention; sham and content-only restoration do not.
hypotheses.target: Holding event content fixed, represented ownership changes a self-history representation; that change causes a present-state change; the present state changes option-specific future predictions and values; those values change present choice.

registered_panel.expansion_order: family order S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6,P_CLAMP,Q_CLAMP; within a family use listed content order, then listed goal order, then NORMAL before REVERSED

thresholds.required_case_success: all expanded cases; no positive-subset scoring
